Where is Silver Beach on Koh Samui? | Silver Beach is on the east coast between Chaweng Noi and Lamai, just off the ring road at GPS 9.4778, 100.0663: 4.6 km north of central Lamai and about 8 km south of Chaweng.
Is Silver Beach the same as Crystal Bay? | Yes, Silver Beach and Crystal Bay are two names for the same small cove; the names come from the two resorts behind it, Silver Beach Resort and Crystal Bay Beach Resort.
Is Silver Beach good for snorkelling? | It is good for easy shore snorkelling along the boulders at both ends, with small reef fish in shallow water, but there is no real coral garden; for reefs, Koh Tan off the south-west coast is much better.
Is there parking at Silver Beach? | There is no public car park; small private lots near the entrance charged about 20 THB for a scooter and 80 THB for a car in late 2025, and a few free spaces exist along the ring road.
When is Silver Beach least crowded? | Before about 09:30 and after 16:00; from 10:00 to mid-afternoon the sunbeds fill up, especially in July–August and from late December to January.
Is Silver Beach safe in the rainy season? | From October to December, and during cold-air surges in January–February, waves roll straight into the cove and red flags go up, so swim only on calm days and stay off the rocks.
Does Silver Beach have toilets and showers? | There are no public toilets or showers; the beachfront restaurants let paying customers use theirs, so buy a drink or lunch.
Can I walk from Lamai to Silver Beach? | It is 4.6 km along the ring road with steep climbs, narrow verges and fast traffic, so a scooter, Grab or songthaew is safer than walking.
Is Silver Beach good for children? | In calm months it is one of the better east-coast coves for children thanks to the gentle sandy entry, but watch for underwater rocks at low tide and bring water shoes.
How long should I spend at Silver Beach? | Two to three hours is enough for a swim, snorkel and lunch; pair it with Coral Cove and the Lad Koh viewpoint, both within 3 km, for a half-day loop.
What should I bring to Silver Beach? | A mask and snorkel, water shoes for the rocky edges, reef-safe sunscreen and cash for parking, sunbeds (about 100 THB) and drinks, as there is no ATM at the cove.
Is Silver Beach better than Lamai Beach? | For a short swim and snorkel in clear water, yes; for space, cheaper food, nightlife and a long walk on the sand, Lamai, 4.6 km south, is the better base.
